summary: Breakdown of the FCNR(B) deposit scheme: brochures advertised 10-15% USD IRR (via leverage) vs ~5% on US Treasuries; actual base returns were ~6-6.5%, the 14% claims were irresponsible marketing, leverage terms can change, and deposit insurance caps at Rs 5 lakh. RBI's real motive: INR was near 94.5-96 (accelerating depreciation, 100 was a psychological line), plus oil-price shock, weak private capex and a consumption slowdown - the scheme buys 3-5 years of forex stability and time to revive growth, not a genius 'short the dollar' trade (the dollar-depreciation story is, in his words, 'quite stupid' given sovereign-gold-bond losses). Verdict: NRIs should NOT pile in - risk not worth the marginal pickup, better opportunities elsewhere; resident Indians should treat this as a telltale sign to diversify (LRS limits could be cut if it fails, down from the current Rs 2.5 cr/yr) - start buying US stocks, and hold some physical gold (not ETFs) as an INR hedge. Calls: none at ticker level - gold and US equities are asset-level views.
